DIAPHRAGM WALLS

What a Useful Diaphragm Wall Handover Package Looks Like

Organise the evidence so the next project team can actually use it.

In this insight

Design the handover before constructionConnect records to locationsSeparate status from appearanceTransfer knowledge as well as filesFor your project discussionDiscuss a project ↗

Educational overview · Project-specific design and execution require qualified review.

Design the handover before construction

Handover should not begin when the final panel is completed. Agree the document index at the start of the package and link it to the contract requirements. The index should identify expected records, review responsibilities and submission milestones. This gives the delivery team time to collect information in the right format and prevents completion from becoming an exercise in chasing disconnected files.

Connect records to locations

Use consistent panel identifiers and drawing references across the package. Include a clear route from the as-built information to the associated construction and inspection records required by the specification. Where deviations were reviewed, retain the approved disposition. A summary sheet can help readers navigate, but it should not replace the underlying evidence or conceal an unresolved issue.

Separate status from appearance

A polished folder is not necessarily a complete handover. Label documents as submitted, reviewed, accepted or awaiting action according to the agreed workflow. Maintain a visible list of outstanding items and their impact on subsequent work. Avoid describing the package as complete while essential approvals remain open; accurate status is more valuable to the receiving team than a reassuring cover page.

Transfer knowledge as well as files

Hold a focused handover meeting with the teams responsible for the next construction stage and the finished asset. Explain the document structure, relevant interfaces and remaining actions. Record questions that require technical clarification. The objective is continuity: a person joining later should be able to understand the wall package without reconstructing months of site conversations from scattered emails.

For your project discussion

Use these questions to structure a conversation with the project’s qualified design and delivery team. This article is general procurement guidance, not a site-specific design, method statement or compliance assessment. The cited international resources provide background; applicable local requirements and the approved project documents govern the work.

Take this into your next conversation

  • Agree the document index at mobilisation.
  • Link evidence to panel locations.
  • Make outstanding items visible to the receiving team.
